Excerpt, scene, or explanation supporting the record:

Yara explains that Lev was assigned to become the wife of a Seraphite elder, although Lev wanted to occupy the masculine role of a soldier. Lev shaved his head, adopted his current name, and fled with Yara after the community rejected him.

During Lev and Abby’s journey, Seraphite enemies call Lev by his former name. Lev later asks Abby whether she wants to discuss what happened. Abby asks whether Lev wants to talk about it, and she respects his decision when he says that he does not.

In the official podcast, Ian Alexander discusses how Lev breaks with the rigidly gendered expectations of his religious upbringing because he can no longer live in a way that conflicts with his identity.

Lev’s transgender identity is central to part of his conflict, but it is not his only narrative characteristic. He is also an archer, survivor, younger brother, religious dissident, companion to Abby, and an important influence on Abby’s later decisions.

For the original 2020 campaign, classify Lev as a supporting character and non-playable ally controlled by the game’s artificial intelligence.

One of the sub-bosses in Streets of Rage III (also released as Bare Knuckle III) is Ash, who is widely described as a very stereotypical gay character. He is dressed as a leather daddy, and wears the female/Venus symbol on a necklace. He was removed from the PAL and US versions of the game, but still accessible as a playable character through cheat codes. He is also, according to the poster of this video (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9VodBRrU4Nw), one of the stronger characters in the game, though a reader commented to use that: He’s stronger and faster than any other character. This Wikipedia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_themes_in_video_games) also refers to Ash as transsexual villain, because he wears a venus symbol and games effeminate sounds. However, there is no evidence he identifies as female.
